title: Compressed Sensing Cross-Validation with Sparse Projection Matrices

key_takeaways.hierarchy: General JL Isometry drops to 22% at q=0.01, yet Model Selection retains 77-88% accuracy down to q=0.05.
key_takeaways.budget_matching: At equal non-zero budget B=5120, a wide-and-sparse matrix (q=0.05, r=200) achieves 98.0% selection accuracy vs 34.0% for narrow-and-dense (q=1.0, r=10).
key_takeaways.kurtosis_theory: Dense Rademacher (gamma=0) strictly achieves lower estimation variance than Dense Gaussian (gamma=2/r^2), confirming Zhang et al. (2014).
key_takeaways.dimension_invariance: Validation sparsity requirements are governed by signal sparsity s, remaining invariant as ambient dimension N quadruples from 256 to 1024.
